claim: per-step relative displacement 2*v_max*dt = 2 m (report)
per-step relative displacement is smaller than d_safe
note: the separation constraint is resolvable at the sample rate

claim: head-on braking distance at a=2 m/s^2 is 25 m (5x d_safe)
note: the discrete mask enforces sample-time separation, not braking; this is a stated limitation of the discrete-time abstraction

claim: the four corner coverage discs are pairwise disjoint, so K-covering the REGION needs N >= 4K
measured: corner separation 80 m vs 2*R_cov = 70 m -> N >= 8 (4K), available 5
expected: N >= 4K with the corner discs disjoint
note: the region requirement. It does NOT transfer to the sensor set: the sensors need not be near the corners, so the applicable bound is the packing bound below.

claim: the region bound N >= 4K is TIGHT at these parameters (a construction with 4K discs K-covers the square)
measured: the worst covered point is 34.875 m from its nearest of the 8 disc centres; R_cov = 35 m (cell half-diagonal 28.28 m, margin 6.72 m)
note: so N = 4K is not merely a lower bound at these parameters: it is the exact minimum for K-covering the region.

claim: the packing bound applied to the realised sensor set excludes N=5 for a MINORITY of random draws, not for all
measured: packing number P mean 2.13 (range 2..3); N >= K*P mean 4.27 (range 4..6); N=5 excluded for 4 of 30 draws (13%)
note: the corner certificate is a statement about the REGION and does not transfer to a random sensor draw; the report says so.

claim: the corner-cap radius at which one sensor per corner still gives pairwise disjoint coverage discs is (side - 2 R_cov)/2, and the grid check confirms the bound is tight
measured: the cap radius is 5.0000 m and the formula gives 5.0000 m; at that radius the closest two points in different caps are 70.0000 m apart, and 2 R_cov = 70.0 m, so the bound is tight
expected: the cap radius equals (side - 2 R_cov)/2 and the grid minimum separation equals 2 R_cov
note: the corner certificate transfers to a sensor set only through a sufficient condition, and the paper says so.

claim: the probability that a uniform draw of M sensors lands one in each of the four corner caps is the order the report quotes
measured: the probability is 9.339e-06 for 20 uniform sensors over a cap of radius 5.00 m (0.3068% of the square)
note: a random sensor draw essentially never meets the corner condition, which is why the region certificate does not transfer.

claim: the achievability construction is admissible under the simulator's own safety filter (so the ceiling is reachable)
measured: the 4K-disc construction is connected, has no articulation point and has eccentricity 3, within the H = 3 rule
note: an achievability ceiling that the safety filter forbids would not be comparable with what a policy can achieve.

claim: the safety filter does not leak: the graph is connected at every step in which the active set is unchanged
measured: 0 disconnections with every UAV active over 2000 steps driven by a uniformly random policy
note: a connectivity availability below 1.000 in the results therefore coincides with UAVs LEAVING the active set (a failure, or a pack that empties away from a pad), not with the filter failing.

claim: the H-hop rule excludes a covering configuration the paper's certificate admits (the 8-node ring)
measured: the 8-node ring is connected and articulation-free but has eccentricity 4 > H = 3
note: the safety filter shrinks the reachable configuration set; a controller that needs to move into a rejected family is stuck. Reported as a property of the filter, not of the task.

claim: z0=50 m with 74 deg FOV yields footprint half-width ~37 m
note: R_cov=35 m is a consistent camera footprint

claim: coverage area ratio N*pi*R^2 / (K*Area) > 1 (necessary)
note: supplied 30,788 m^2, required 12,800 m^2

claim: area ratio still > 1 after one UAV fails
note: reserve is a safety factor, not the only route to feasibility

claim: counting bound R_cov >= sqrt(K*Area/(pi*N))
area surplus sigma = N*pi*R^2/A is NOT a feasibility criterion (report claim)
measured: sigma=4.811
expected: sigma>1 is NOT sufficient for feasibility
note: sigma is an area ratio; a positive sigma does not imply a covering exists (this is the report's stated finding)

claim: corner separation S=80 m exceeds 2*R_cov=70 m, so the four corner K-cover discs are pairwise disjoint
B_max/P_hover endurance is 600 s (10 min)
note: the report's B_max=30 kJ with P_hover=50 W

claim: B_max corresponds to a real pack of this class
measured: 8.33 Wh (600 s = 10 min hover)
expected: DJI Mini 3 18.1 Wh, Mavic 2 43.6 Wh, Phantom 4 Pro 89.2 Wh
note: the report explicitly states these are simulator parameters rather than experimentally calibrated real-flight values; FINDINGS C14a suggests 60 kJ for a 20 min self-consistent endurance, which would change the reported energy figures and is left as a stated limitation

claim: P_move/P_hover ratio is physically plausible
note: FINDINGS C14b; a 1.5 ratio is conservative for forward flight of a multirotor at 5 m/s, and the report disclaims flight calibration

claim: charge rate corresponds to a plausible C-rate
measured: 3.60 C (30 W, full charge in 1000 s)
note: the report states the charge increment is a modelling assumption rather than a physical prediction

claim: the battery DOES drain over the episode used for the reported results, so the return-to-charge transition, the charging arbitration and the reserve mechanism are exercised rather than inert
measured: 20,000 J of 30,000 J (66.7%) over 2000 steps of hovering
note: at the earlier 400-step episode the drain was only 4,000 J (13.3%), so the return state never fired and the energy machinery was inert; the reported configuration uses 2000 steps instead. Over the report's full 10,000-step target the drain would be 100,000 J (333% of the pack).

claim: R_comm = 40 m does not make connectivity trivial
measured: mean node degree 4.25 on a 3x3 grid (spacing 26.7 m < R_comm = 40 m)
expected: < 2.0 for connectivity to be the binding constraint
note: FINDINGS C14f. At N=8 on an 80x80 m field the inter-UAV graph is dense, so R_comm does not bind in the nominal deployment. Connectivity becomes the binding constraint only after a failure removes one UAV, which is exactly the regime the H=3-step feasibility mask and the reserve mechanism protect. This is reported as a stated design condition rather than a claim of a hard connectivity constraint.

claim: the connectivity constraint is live in the deployed regime
measured: mean node degree 3.63 of a possible 7; the graph was complete in 12.0% of steps; 22.6% of UAV-steps left a node of degree <= 1
expected: < 7.00 (the graph must not be complete throughout)
note: measured on a 2000-step flight in the clustered deployment, the configuration the experiments use. The graph is not complete throughout, so a single UAV can be critical and the H-step feasibility mask and the reserve mechanism are load-bearing rather than decorative.

claim: LoS probability at z0=50 m over 80 m is high
note: geometry, not path loss, is the binding constraint

claim: noise power for 20 MHz / NF 7 dB is ~4e-13 W
SNR margin at R_comm=40 m (free space, 0.5 W TX) is positive
measured: 46.8 dB (SNR 48.8 dB vs threshold 2.0 dB)
note: geometry, not path loss, binds the connectivity constraint

claim: Python log_distance_pl and INET BreakpointPathLoss are the same function (max |delta| <= 0.1 dB)
measured: max |delta| = 0.0120 dB over 24 (distance, exponent) points
note: model equivalence proven from INET's source and the parameters recorded by the OMNeT++ run

claim: the OMNeT++/INET PHY scenario produced a scalar result file (Phase 2 executed)
measured: phy_validation_0.sca present
note: the 802.11 stack is executable end to end; the per-link physical observable is discussed in the report

claim: the teleporting oracle finds a feasible K=2 placement for N=8
measured: oracle CK (connected) = 1.000, SC reachable = True
note: achievability ceiling for the trained policy

claim: the evaluation of a sampled policy is a function of (policy, scene) and does not depend on the ambient state of the global RNG; the sampling stream is seeded from the evaluation seed alone, so every controller is measured on the same stream on the same scene
measured: CK=1.0 and Energy=3604.0 and Distance=188.0 and CovIntegral=0.0  |  CK=1.0 and Energy=3604.0 and Distance=188.0 and CovIntegral=0.0
note: the policy samples, so the sampling stream is seeded from the evaluation seed; every controller therefore sees the same stream on the same scene

claim: on the provably infeasible N=5 configuration the coverage ratio is NOT small, so a reader without an achievability reference cannot tell the instance from a feasible one
measured: CK = 0.648 with AG = 1.000, SC = 0.000, and the teleporting oracle reaches CK = 0.990 on the same scenes
note: the twenty sensors are coverable, so the coverage shortfall is the controller's; the certificate, and not either metric, is what says the REGION is not coverable at N = 5

claim: no disconnection of the communication graph is left by a policy action: the safety filter and the joint projection maintain connectivity across every action
measured: 6 transitions into a disconnected graph over the whole evaluation matrix, of which 0 are attributable to a policy action and the rest to a UAV leaving the active set
note: the guarantee is about actions; the availability below 1.000 is the recovery mechanism's signature, and the accounting counts transitions, because a graph that is already disconnected stays disconnected

claim: the alternative corrected deployment N=5, K=2, R_cov=45 m really does K-cover the region: four discs at the side midpoints and one at the centre cover every point of the square at least twice
measured: the worst second-nearest distance over the square is 44.72 m, against the 45 m radius offered
note: the paper's threshold for this deployment is the radius the construction needs; the construction is the witness that the deployment is feasible

claim: a training run is reproducible from its seed on a fixed device: the seed is set before the networks are constructed, so the initialisation is seeded too.  The device and the thread count are part of the protocol, because the floating-point kernels and the order of the reductions differ between them, and two runs of the same configuration that happen to land on different devices are not the same experiment
measured: max |difference| over the trained parameters = 0
note: the seed is set at the start of train_mappo, before the actor and the critic are built, so the initial weights do not depend on the ambient state of the global RNG
